This is first appeal filed under Section 14-A (2) of the Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (in short "SC/ST Act") against the order dated 22.12.2023 passed by the Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Dhar in B.A. No.212/2023, whereby the application filed by the appellant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been dismissed in connection with FIR/Crime No.813/2023 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station - Pithampur Sector No.1, District - Dhar for commission of offence punishable under Sections 366, 376 and 506 of IPC alongwith 3(1)(wii), 3(2) and 3(2)(va) of the SC/ST Act.

sentences.text: 2. Prosecution story in brief is that on 10.09.2023, when the prosecutrix was returning from her coaching class, appellant met her and after threatening, took her to his room thereafter, he again threatened her on the point of knife and committed rape upon her.
Thereafter, prosecutrix returned back to her home but due to fear, she did not narrate the incident to her family members.
On 24.11.2023, prosecutrix lodged a report against the appellant.
3 . Learned counsel for the appellant/accused submits that the appellant has not committed the offence and he has falsely been implicated in the case.
Prosecutrix is a major lady.
The report was lodged after a delay of 02 months without any plausible explanation.
Appellant has no criminal past and he is in custody since 24.11.2023.
After completion of investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.
Conclusion of trial will take considerable long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that appellant may be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State as well as counsel for the objector have opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection.

5. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, coupled with the fact that trial of the case will take considerable time for its disposal, therefore, this Court is of the view that it is a fit case to grant regular bail to the appellant.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and impugned order dated 22.12.2023 is set aside.

6. It is directed that the appellant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court with a direction that he will cooperate in trial and present himself regularly before the Trial Court on each and every date fixed by the Court concerned during trial and if during trial, he is found absent without any sufficient cause by the Trial Court, then the bail order passed by this Court shall automatically come to an end without reference to the Court.
7. With the aforesaid, present criminal appeal stands allowed and disposed of.
Certified copy, as per Rules.
